name: gcc_c89
description: GCC on modern Unix-like systems, strict ANSI C89 baseline
compile_command: gcc -std=c89 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -pthread -DFAX_WITH_PNG -DFAX_WITH_JPEG -DFAX_WITH_TIFF $(pkg-config --cflags libpng libjpeg libtiff-4) fax_core.c fax_engine.c fax_g3.c fax_image.c fax_tables.c fax_thread.c fax_default_params.c fax_engine_test.c -lm $(pkg-config --libs libpng libjpeg libtiff-4) -o fax_engine_test
notes: Strict C89 build; no C99 headers or syntax are required.
The caller supplies image buffers and two row work buffers.
The engine performs no heap allocation; the host supplies its workspace. The convenience test driver uses malloc and standard file I/O.
The optimizer and image transforms use C math functions (pow, exp, sqrt, floor, fmod); ensure the toolchain links its math runtime.
The CLI decodes PGM/BMP internally and uses libpng/libjpeg/libtiff APIs in-process for PNG/JPEG/TIFF. No image converter subprocess or intermediate PGM is created.

The decoder libraries are linked into the same process. Use static codec archives and static-link flags if a self-contained executable is required; shared-library linking does not start separate converter processes.
TIFF accepts a zero-based directory/page argument. TIFF planar-separate images are rejected explicitly; all eight TIFF orientations are normalized. CMYK/YCCK JPEG is rejected explicitly.
For a build without PNG/JPEG/TIFF dependencies, omit FAX_WITH_* defines and codec libraries; built-in PGM and BMP remain available.
cpu_architecture: host compiler target; select x86/x64/ARM through GCC target options
endianness: native compiler target; no byte-order assumptions in the core
